units.translation: Phrynichus in Bekker p. 73, 10. Ψυχαγωγός [conjurer of souls]: the ancients called those who lead (or bring up, Nauck) the souls of the dead by certain enchantments. Of the same meaning is also the play of Aeschylus (fr. 269-275).
raising shrill laments with soul-conjuring wails.

Never did I think that such hard-to-see and hard-to-bear sufferings would rub my soul.
Therefore, willing, she shares in evils with an unwilling partner, my soul.
Terrible are they in battle, with steadfast resolve of soul.
And they are best in soul and conspicuous in noble birth.
